whatItFakes: The working life before the start runs in the person's day-one town, against its businesses' day-one size and going pay and the nation's unemployment rate; a spell before a person's move into the county runs where they lived then with no employer named (the world keeps none there), and officials living outside the town are not run.
why: Moves before the start, past business sizes and the regional series are not yet simulated before the start; the unit that runs them replaces each part.
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: the regional economy series in the economy pass, business sizes from the business pass's history, and history-past-officials for officials' careers.
resolvedBy: stand-in triage T9 (owner, Nov 10: too in depth)

whatItFakes: A move into the county before the start is dated by the moves engine's life-stage rate and the hold of children at home only: a lost job, owning a home, relatives in town and the person's own temperament, which push or hold in play, do not move it; whether someone came is read only from a parent living outside the county or a recorded birthplace outside it, so a person whose parents died long ago never came.
why: The working-life run (which records the layoffs) runs after the moves, since it places each spell where the person lived; the years before the start run general, with no depth (owner, Oct 28, 2026).
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: Run moves and the working life together, quarter by quarter, so a layoff pushes a move as the moves engine's work.job-lost pull does in play; record where each person grew up when the opening generates their family.
resolvedBy: stand-in triage T9 (owner, Nov 10: too in depth)

whatItFakes: A school year in a place with no public school district record (a place the world does not keep, or a town whose opening has no police department to copy the district from) is recorded against the place's schools as the place itself, with no name, so the Journal, the person card and talk leave it out.
why: The school engine's own rule names the district of the place; only the town's district is an organization, and real campus names are not shown as themselves (owner, Oct 27: real data only calibrates).
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: Every place a person can have lived keeps its schools at a coarser level (AGENTS.md: other places at a coarser level), each with a generated name from the place's records, and every town opens with its district.
resolvedBy: stand-in triage T9 (owner, Nov 10: too in depth)

whatItFakes: A couple among people filled in from the counts is told from who shares a home and a child (two grown members of one household who are both kin to the child at home), because the counted columns record shared homes but not who is partnered; a couple with no child at home, or a household of several grown kin, is not told, and a former partner is never told.
why: The counted population keeps no individual past (two-level population); the card must tell a spouse who exists without inventing one, and the household is the record that says who lives with whom (owner, Oct 28, 14:50: the one history from the birth year, coarse and general).
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: Carry the partnership in the counted household record when the opening generates it, with the day it began, so fill-in reads it instead of inferring it.
resolvedBy: stand-in triage T9 (owner, Nov 10: too in depth)

whatItFakes: Every adult whose opening profile gives a schooling level is told as finishing high school on their class's day, including the adults without a diploma, because the opening profile's levels (CES 2024: no-college, some-college, college) fold them into no-college.
why: Gap sheet, Nov 12, row 15: a past had school starts and never an end. The profile is the one record of a person's schooling, and the work pass already dates a first job from the same day.
replacement: Split no-college into less than high school and a diploma by the ACS educational attainment shares by age (table B15001), on the profile itself, so the school pass, the work pass and the jobs engine read the same level.

whatItFakes: An arrest before the start comes from age alone, from 13 to 23, at the national share: the person's sex, traits, place, schooling and household do not weigh, no arrest after 23 is written, every conviction is a felony a year after the arrest, and every prison term is two years.
why: Gap sheet, Nov 12, row 4: a past never held an arrest. The national cumulative shares (Brame et al. 2012; Shannon et al. 2017) were the published figures read.
replacement: Arrest by sex and race-blind household income from Brame et al. (2014, Crime & Delinquency 60(3)), weighed by the person's traits through the shared trait table, with misdemeanor convictions and sentence lengths from BJS Felony Sentences in State Courts.

whatItFakes: The player's own past is run by the same rule as everyone's, so about three players in ten start with an arrest by 23 in their history, and some with a conviction, told on their own card and Journal.
why: One rule for every person; whether the player's own character may start with a criminal record is a call about the player's experience, which only the owner makes (AGENTS.md, 'This is a game, not a spreadsheet').
replacement: Decided Nov 12, 2026 (owner, 6:33 p.m., passed on by the CTO on #8928): the player's own past follows the same rule as everyone's, so it can hold an arrest, a conviction or a prison term. Choosing one's past through scenes after early access is the item core-life-record-part-16-choose-your-past-through-scenes.

whatItFakes: Every veteran served one first term of the same length (pastServiceYears, four years) from the day their schooling ended: no draft-era two-year service, no officer after college, no career of twenty years, no branch, no deployment, and no Reserve or Guard.
why: Gap sheet, Nov 12, row 4: no past held military service. The ACS share says who served; how long and where needs its own research.
replacement: Service length and branch by cohort from the VA's National Survey of Veterans or the Defense Manpower Data Center's separations, with draft-era terms for those born before 1953, read against the person's traits.

whatItFakes: A move inside the county before the start is written on the adult's own past with the children at home named in its facts, but a child's own past, written when the child is opened, does not hold the moves they made with that parent.
why: Gap sheet, Nov 12, row 16: a past held at most one move. The within-county moves run per adult from their own seeded line; a child's own run would need the parent's moves read first.
replacement: When a child is opened, read the moves of the parent they lived with (by the record's childIds) into the child's own past instead of running their own until they are grown.

whatItFakes: Every person the opening makes is given a birthplace fact naming the town they live in now (no caller passes a birthplace), so the fact never names anywhere else: 0 of 476 residents in Portsmouth NH, Selma NC and Woodlawn KY (seeds lrborn01 to 03) were born elsewhere by it. Readers that tell a birthplace (the card, a conversation) take the moves pass's residence on the birth date first, so a person brought to the county is born where they came from.
why: The opening runs before the past's moves, which decide who came from elsewhere; the card told 'born in' the town and then 'moved to' it (Fable A, Nov 13).
replacement: Write the birthplace fact from the moves pass (the residence on the birth date) when a person's past is opened, by the ACS share born in their state of residence (B05002) for those with no parent elsewhere, and drop the opening's default.
